text:
sara: Heads-up — customer reported 403 on /v1/generate, message: "signature verification failed". Customer on Dedicated cluster eu-west-1. They rotated service keys yesterday. Request-ID: req_3f9a2b7c.
jen (SE): Can you paste the raw curl they used and the failing request-id from the logs? we'll need headers + body to repro.

sara: Pasting their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-987" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'
```
They said the token is a service token, but header used is X-Redwood-Project. They also tried with x-org header but got same result.

ajay: Looking at the backend logs for req_3f9a2b7c we see: `signature_check: failure, missing_signed_header: x-org-id` and `signed_headers=\"(request-target) host date authorization\"`. That explains signature mismatch — signer didn't include x-org-id in signed headers.

sara: Server log snippet:
```
[2026-02-10T14:21:03Z] req=req_3f9a2b7c auth=svc_45 error="signature verification failed" details="missing_signed_header: x-org-id"
```

ops-bot: Debug bundle created: dbg-1768509123-3f9a2b7c (link: https://internal.redwood/debug/dbg-1768509123) :white_check_mark:

ajay: My hunch — SDK v2.4.0 changed canonical header name from X-Redwood-Org to X-Redwood-Project and the signer lib didn't add the new header into the signature header list. Two paths: reproduce with a curl that signs including x-org-id, or have SDK emit fallback header.

nate: Confirmed — runtime change note in changelog: "rename X-Redwood-Org -> X-Redwood-Project" (v2.4.0). If customer's client rotates keys but still signs canonical headers expecting x-org-id, signature mismatch happens.

ajay: Quick repro curl to try from eng machine (explicitly include x-org-id in signed headers):
```
# Assuming service key signed token model; this forces x-org-id header
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_45.signature-token" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'
```
If that succeeds, the issue is header canonicalization. If it still 403s, capture full `-v` output and send here with the request-id.

jen (SE): Customer says their environment uses SDK v2.4.0 and they don't control header mapping easily. Short mitigation: proxy rewrite rule to map X-Redwood-Project -> X-Redwood-Org for requests coming from their IPs. Can SRE/infra add that temporarily?

ajay: I can add a temporary header rewrite for that customer on the ingress rule today. Before I do, need the failing request timestamp and IP. Sara — can you ask customer to replay the failing request (same token) so we get a new req-id we can watch? Also include exact SDK version string and platform.

sara: On it. Asked for: (1) full curl -v, (2) SDK version, (3) failing request-id (if they still have it) or permission to replay, (4) their public egress IP.

nate: Long-term, we should make signer robust to header aliases or add a compatibility shim in the auth layer. Filing a follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:

ajay: TL;DR: probable canonical-header mismatch due to header rename in SDK. Repro steps above. I'll apply ingress rewrite after customer replays and we get a fresh req ID to correlate.

sara: Customer replied with new req id req_7b1c4a55 and gave IP 35.204.12.9 — forwarding to ajay.

jen (SE): Thanks — keeping customer updated that we're on it.

ajay: Got the new req id, tailing logs now...

sara: Thanks all. Will follow up when ingress rewrite is in place or if repro fails.
